summary: RemedialFlow pre-deployment final check (iter 16). New file /app/backend/tests/test_final_csrf_push.py (17 tests) — all GREEN against live preview URL. Covers: (1) CSRF for cookie-authenticated web endpoints — web login with X-Client:web sets rf_refresh cookie, no body refresh_token; refresh with cookie but NO X-Client -> 403; refresh with cookie + Origin https://evil.example -> 403; refresh with X-Client:web + own origin -> 200 with rotated cookie; native body refresh (X-Client:native + refresh_token in body) still -> 200 unaffected; logout obeys the same CSRF rules; backend emits SameSite=strict/HttpOnly/Secure (confirmed via internal :8001). (2) Push: /api/register-push no auth -> 401; invalid platform -> 422; placeholder EMERGENT_PUSH_KEY -> clean 500/502 without crash; user_id spoofed in body is IGNORED (verified in db — the other user's push_active was NOT flipped); /api/unregister-push -> 200 and users.push_active=false. Assigning an NC via /ncs/{id}/assign returned in <2s (not blocked by failing push upstream) AND wrote the 'assigned' in-app notification for the newly-assigned installer; disabled installer -> assign refused 400 and zero notifications written for that user. (3) SEC-001: change-password response includes fresh access_token (+ refresh_token on native); old refresh now 401 on /auth/refresh; old access now 401 on /auth/me (token_version bumped); new access & new refresh both 200. Test performed on a scratch TEST_cp_*@example.com installer (demo creds untouched). (4) discard_evidence NC-scoped: installer2 DELETE /api/evidence/{fid} of installer1 draft -> 403; owner installer1 -> 200. Full regression `pytest tests/ -q` ran 232 passed + 4 skipped + 1 ConnectTimeout flake (test_approved_nc_rejects_upload; passes in isolation — same known preview-URL congestion flake E1 described). Frontend (390x844): installer login OK; page reload keeps session (cookie refresh path works); Account screen renders change-password + logout; change-password sheet opens with current & new inputs; expo-notifications emits an informational web warning only ('Listening to push token changes not yet fully supported on web'), NO red screen / no crash. Cleanup: db.rate_limits cleared via session fixture; TEST_cp_*/TEST_dis_* users deleted; demo passwords untouched. INFORMATIONAL: the Kubernetes ingress rewrites the Set-Cookie to 'SameSite=None; Partitioned' before it reaches the browser via the public preview URL, even though the backend emits 'SameSite=Strict' — on the preview URL the SameSite defense is NOT in effect; CSRF still holds via the X-Client:web header (preflight) + Origin allowlist. E1 should confirm the production ingress preserves SameSite=Strict (or accept the 2 remaining layers).

minor.issue: Backend emits SameSite=Strict (verified on :8001) but the preview-URL ingress rewrites it to SameSite=None; Partitioned. CSRF defense remains intact via X-Client header + Origin allowlist (both tested). Confirm production ingress preserves Strict.

action_items: No functional action items — all 17 new tests pass and full regression is clean modulo the 1 known preview-URL ConnectTimeout flake (passes in isolation).

Informational: verify the production deployment ingress does NOT rewrite rf_refresh's SameSite attribute from Strict to None. If it does, the preview behaviour will reach production and the Strict layer will be inert (defense still holds via X-Client + Origin, so this is not blocking).
critical_code_review_comments: auth.py:79 cookie_session() — guard runs ONLY when a cookie is present, so native-body refresh is untouched. Verified behaviourally (test_native_refresh_with_body_unaffected).

auth.py:255 change_password now bumps token_version, revokes all sessions, then returns fresh tokens via token_payload(). Native receives refresh_token in body; web receives rotated cookie. Verified end-to-end against a TEST user: old refresh -> 401, old access -> 401, new access -> 200.

push.py:35 register_push correctly derives user_id from the authenticated token (u.id). Any user_id in the body is a free-form field on the Pydantic model and is IGNORED — confirmed by inspecting the other user's push_active flag post-call (still unset).

push.py:74 push_for() uses find_one({active:true, push_active:true}) short-circuit AND the whole send is wrapped in try/except, so a 5xx from the relay (placeholder key) never crashes notify(). Verified: /ncs/{id}/assign returned in <2s and still wrote the in-app notification row.
server.py:109 notify() short-circuits on {active:true}. test_disabled_installer_gets_no_new_notification confirms zero rows written for a deactivated user.

server.py:819 discard_evidence now calls await get_nc(f.nc_id, u) BEFORE the owner check — this is the NC-scoped guard that returns 403 for installer2 even though the earlier draft/owner checks could leak existence. Correct ordering.

frontend/src/api.ts:49 login always sends X-Client:'web' on web and 'native' on native; logout and refreshSession both send the same header. The CSRF cookie path is exercised correctly from the real frontend (page reload keeps the session).

frontend/src/push.ts:7 registerForPush() short-circuits on Platform.OS==='web' || !Device.isDevice — expo-notifications therefore cannot throw during web preview boot. Verified (only an informational 'push token changes not supported on web' warning, no crash).
